name: Ranger 7–9
location_summary: Three separate lunar impact sites for Rangers 7, 8, and 9.
objective: Return increasingly detailed images during final approach to the Moon.
science_summary: The successful Rangers transmitted close-range lunar imagery before impact, improving knowledge of surface features before crewed landings.
story_hook: They learned by looking all the way down.

name: Lunar Orbiter 1–5
location_summary: The five orbiters completed lunar mapping missions and were disposed of by lunar impact.
objective: Photograph possible Apollo landing sites and expand lunar mapping coverage.
science_summary: Five missions photographed nearly all of the Moon and provided high-resolution views used for landing-site assessment.
story_hook: Before astronauts chose a path, orbiters drew the map.

name: Surveyor 1
location_summary: Oceanus Procellarum, on the lunar near side.
objective: Demonstrate a controlled soft landing and return images and engineering data.
science_summary: Surveyor 1 achieved the first successful U.S. lunar soft landing and returned thousands of surface images while demonstrating technology needed for later landings.
story_hook: A machine learning how to touch another world gently.

name: Surveyor 3
location_summary: Mare Cognitum; Apollo 12 later landed nearby and visited the spacecraft.
objective: Study the lunar surface and demonstrate landing technology.
science_summary: Surveyor 3 photographed and sampled the surface; Apollo 12 astronauts later retrieved parts for study of long exposure to the lunar environment.
story_hook: The robot that astronauts met on the Moon.

name: Apollo 11 Surface Hardware
location_summary: Mare Tranquillitatis; the descent stage and experiment hardware remain at the landing site.
objective: Support the first crewed lunar landing and deploy early surface experiments.
science_summary: The laser-ranging retroreflector remains a passive target for precise Earth–Moon distance measurements; other early experiment hardware completed its operations.
story_hook: A mirror with no power can still answer Earth.

name: Apollo 12 Surface Hardware
location_summary: Oceanus Procellarum near Surveyor 3.
objective: Perform a precision landing, collect samples, visit Surveyor 3, and deploy long-duration experiments.
science_summary: Apollo 12 demonstrated precise landing and deployed an experiment station that contributed years of lunar environmental and geophysical observations.
story_hook: A human landing guided to an earlier robot.

name: Apollo 14 Surface Hardware
location_summary: Fra Mauro formation.
objective: Study Fra Mauro geology and deploy surface experiments.
science_summary: Apollo 14 returned samples, deployed a long-duration experiment package, and left a retroreflector used for lunar ranging.
story_hook: Geology and a returning beam of light at Fra Mauro.

name: Apollo 15 Surface Hardware
hardware_types: lunar module descent stage|lunar rover|ALSEP|passive retroreflector
location_summary: Hadley–Apennine region.
objective: Expand lunar field geology using the first Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle.
science_summary: The rover extended traverse range, while surface experiments and a retroreflector supported geophysical and ranging science.
story_hook: The first wheels that carried people across the Moon.

name: Apollo 16 Surface Hardware
location_summary: Descartes Highlands.
objective: Investigate lunar highlands geology and deploy surface experiments.
science_summary: Apollo 16 used rover-supported fieldwork and instruments to examine highlands materials and the lunar environment.
story_hook: A rover crossing terrain scientists once expected to be volcanic.

name: Apollo 17 Surface Hardware
location_summary: Taurus–Littrow valley.
objective: Conduct extended geological exploration and deploy surface experiments.
science_summary: The rover enabled more than 30 kilometers of traverses and helped the crew collect a large, diverse sample set across Taurus–Littrow.
story_hook: Mobility turned a landing site into a field laboratory.

name: Viking 1
location_summary: Viking 1 lander remains in Chryse Planitia; its orbiter mission ended earlier.
objective: Image Mars, characterize its surface and atmosphere, and search for evidence relevant to life.
science_summary: Viking 1 returned surface images, weather and chemistry measurements, and complex biology-experiment results that require careful, qualified interpretation.
story_hook: A laboratory asked a question whose answer was not simple.

name: Viking 2
location_summary: Viking 2 lander remains in Utopia Planitia; its orbiter mission ended earlier.
objective: Study a second Mars site with imaging, atmosphere, soil, and biology investigations.
science_summary: The second landing site enabled comparison of Martian surface, weather, chemistry, and biology-experiment results.
story_hook: One planet, two laboratories, and a chance to compare.

name: Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner
location_summary: Ares Vallis; the lander and Sojourner rover remain at the site.
objective: Demonstrate a lower-cost landing system and mobile surface exploration.
science_summary: Pathfinder returned imaging, weather, and rock-composition data while Sojourner demonstrated rover operations on Mars.
story_hook: A small rover proved that wheels could explore Mars.

name: Spirit
location_summary: Gusev Crater, near the final location called Troy.
objective: Study rocks and soils for evidence of past water and environmental conditions.
science_summary: Spirit operated far beyond its planned lifetime and found strong evidence that parts of ancient Mars were wetter, including water-related minerals and silica-rich material.
story_hook: A stuck wheel opened a new scientific clue.

name: Opportunity
location_summary: Meridiani Planum, on the rim of Endeavour Crater.
objective: Investigate Martian geology and evidence of past water.
science_summary: Opportunity documented sedimentary rocks and minerals formed or altered in water and traveled more than 45 kilometers before a global dust storm ended communications.
story_hook: A 90-day rover that explored for nearly fifteen years.

name: Phoenix
location_summary: Northern polar plains of Mars, in the Vastitas Borealis region.
objective: Study polar soil, near-surface ice, weather, and habitability-related chemistry.
science_summary: Phoenix exposed and analyzed water ice and measured polar soil and atmospheric conditions.
story_hook: A lander dug into the Martian arctic and found ice.

name: Curiosity
location_summary: Gale Crater, traversing Mount Sharp.
objective: Assess whether Mars ever offered environments habitable to microbial life and study its geology and climate.
science_summary: Curiosity found evidence of ancient habitable lake and stream environments while measuring rocks, atmosphere, radiation, and organic compounds.
story_hook: A rolling laboratory climbs through layers of Martian time.

name: InSight
location_summary: Elysium Planitia.
objective: Study Mars's crust, mantle, core, and present seismic activity.
science_summary: InSight detected marsquakes and produced measurements that constrain the planet's internal structure.
story_hook: A still lander listened to a planet move.

name: Perseverance
location_summary: Jezero Crater and surrounding terrain.
objective: Seek signs of ancient habitable conditions and possible biosignatures, characterize geology, and cache samples.
science_summary: Perseverance investigates an ancient lake-and-delta environment, studies rocks and atmosphere, and collects sealed samples for possible future return.
story_hook: A rover stores carefully chosen pieces of Mars for a possible journey home.

name: Ingenuity
location_summary: Neretva Vallis region in Jezero Crater, at its final airfield.
objective: Demonstrate powered, controlled flight in the Martian atmosphere.
science_summary: Ingenuity completed 72 flights after being designed for five, demonstrating aerial mobility and scouting operations on another planet.
story_hook: Five planned flights became seventy-two.

name: Pioneer 10
location_summary: Traveling outward on an escape trajectory; no longer in communication.
objective: Cross the asteroid belt, investigate Jupiter, and characterize the outer solar-system environment.
science_summary: Pioneer 10 made the first close reconnaissance of Jupiter and demonstrated passage through the asteroid belt and outer solar system.
story_hook: The first spacecraft sent onto a path out of the solar system.

name: Pioneer 11
destination: Jupiter, Saturn, and an escape trajectory
location_summary: Traveling outward on an escape trajectory; no longer in communication.
objective: Investigate Jupiter and conduct the first close reconnaissance of Saturn.
science_summary: Pioneer 11 returned measurements and images from Jupiter and became the first spacecraft to encounter Saturn closely.
story_hook: A pathfinder reached Saturn before Voyager.

name: Voyager 1
location_summary: Traveling through interstellar space beyond the heliopause.
objective: Explore Jupiter and Saturn, then study the outer heliosphere and interstellar environment.
science_summary: Voyager 1 transformed knowledge of Jupiter and Saturn and later became the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space, returning fields-and-particles data under declining power.
story_hook: A planetary explorer became an interstellar weather station.

name: Voyager 2
destination: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and interstellar space
location_summary: Traveling through interstellar space beyond the heliopause.
objective: Conduct the only close reconnaissance of all four giant planets and continue into interstellar space.
science_summary: Voyager 2 remains the only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune and now samples the interstellar environment.
story_hook: One spacecraft completed the grand tour of the giant planets.

name: Galileo
location_summary: The atmospheric probe entered Jupiter in 1995; the orbiter was directed into Jupiter in 2003.
objective: Study Jupiter, its atmosphere, magnetosphere, rings, and major moons.
science_summary: Galileo deployed the first probe into Jupiter's atmosphere and revealed active and potentially ocean-bearing worlds in the Jovian system.
story_hook: An orbiter and a falling probe explored a giant system together.

name: Cassini–Huygens
location_summary: Huygens rests on Titan; Cassini was directed into Saturn at mission end.
objective: Study Saturn, its rings, magnetosphere, and moons; land Huygens on Titan.
science_summary: The mission revealed an active Saturn system, including Titan's atmosphere and surface and Enceladus's plume activity.
story_hook: An orbiter carried a partner lander into Titan's orange haze.

name: NEAR Shoemaker
location_summary: Resting on the surface of asteroid 433 Eros.
objective: Orbit, map, and characterize Eros, then perform a controlled descent.
science_summary: NEAR became the first spacecraft to orbit and land on an asteroid, returning composition, shape, density, and surface data.
story_hook: An orbiter survived a landing it was never built to make.

name: Deep Impact / EPOXI
location_summary: The impactor struck Tempel 1; the flyby spacecraft continued as EPOXI before contact was lost.
objective: Expose and observe subsurface comet material, then extend the spacecraft to additional comet and exoplanet observations.
science_summary: The impact produced a plume observed by the flyby craft and other telescopes, revealing information about comet composition and structure.
story_hook: One spacecraft watched while another made a crater for science.

name: Dawn
location_summary: Remains in a stable orbit around dwarf planet Ceres.
objective: Orbit and compare Vesta and Ceres, two large protoplanetary bodies.
science_summary: Ion propulsion allowed Dawn to orbit two different extraterrestrial targets and compare their geology, composition, and evolution.
story_hook: One spacecraft orbited two worlds.

name: New Horizons
destination: Pluto, Arrokoth, and the Kuiper Belt
location_summary: Traveling outward through the Kuiper Belt region after the Pluto and Arrokoth flybys.
objective: Conduct the first close exploration of Pluto and later study a Kuiper Belt object and distant environment.
science_summary: New Horizons revealed unexpectedly complex Pluto-system geology and later returned the first close observations of Arrokoth.
story_hook: Years of planning for a few fast hours beside Pluto.
